candidates.title: What If A Time Machine Actually Worked?
candidates.hook: He travels back one hour and arrives in empty space.
candidates.visualPromise: An inventor spends everything on a time machine; the test dummy returns with a surprise, a rival tries a bigger one, and the Earth's motion makes every jump land somewhere unexpected.
candidates.whyItWorks: A real physical fact (the Earth moves about 30 km/s around the Sun) turns a familiar sci-fi dream into a visible, funny, escalating consequence told through one inventor's want, cost, test, fix and payoff.

candidates.title: The Giant Pumpkin Launcher
candidates.hook: He builds the biggest launcher in the festival, then hits his own barn.
candidates.visualPromise: Release angle and counterweight decide where a pumpkin lands; a rival's launcher returns it to its owner.
candidates.whyItWorks: Clear anticipation, contact and consequence, with a POV from the projectile.

candidates.title: Why The Bridge Wobbled
candidates.hook: Opening day: everyone steps in time and the bridge starts to sway.
candidates.visualPromise: A builder fixes synchronized sway with dampers while the rival's stiff bridge fails the same test.
candidates.whyItWorks: A real engineering story (London Millennium Bridge, 2000) with a visible mechanism and a rival payoff.
